signature: A red-wood civilisation on an island under a pale pink sky and an everlasting sun: a cove dockyard where arrivals land, cliff watchtowers over a sea that breaks every boat, and behind the mountains the farms, Almond Water river and the timber gathering station of Hyperia

exits.label: Cast off from the T-head in a sloop and sailed into the dead zone; the hull split (every recorded attempt died; Level 114 is only the theoretical landfall)
exits.method: Sail several days away from the island
exits.source_quote: all attempts result in the death of the wanderers
exits.hint: The harbour log lists every departure for the far side. None came back.

exits.label: Cast off from the T-head in the second sloop; the same crossing (Level 284 is the other theoretical landfall)
exits.source_quote: one would theoretically end up in Level 114 or Level 284
exits.hint: Two sloops are kept rigged at the end of the jetty.

fail_states.label: Swam past the cove mouth into the dead zone
fail_states.source_quote: Anything ahead of the boundaries of our island is deemed a dead zone

entity_policy: SOURCED ENTITIES ONLY. The Kraken sleeps far out in the depths and is never shown. The REPORTED sightings of enormous entities outside the island appear only as a dark mass breaking the surface ~1 km offshore, seen from a watchtower deck. No land entities and no NPCs (the page names no individuals; the 25,000 inhabitants are implied by dressing, smoke and sound).
notes: SOURCE: island in vast oceans; rough cliffs and steep slopes of rock and metal; inner mountains feeding wide Almond Water rivers; outer areas / outer circle / inner circle; small wooden towns with large farms and huts between the mountains; huts and watchtowers at elevated places in the outer circle; dead zone past the shore that breaks the strongest boats; red-trunk white-leaf trees, fire-proof wood stronger than aluminium, easily cut with an axe; Hyperia as the trade hub in the middle with office-like diplomatic buildings, a gathering station not a capital; mountains and coastline not habitable; iron and copper in giant cave veins; colourful flowers on the hills and sometimes rainbows; ~25,000 inhabitants, Wanderer Nations without formal names; pale pink sky and everlasting sun; arrival at the dockyards; Kraken asleep far away; only exit is the deadly crossing to Level 114 or 284 (theoretical). ADAPTATION: the 2 166 000 km2 island is compressed to a ~0.5 x 0.6 km playable corridor (cove dockyard -> gully -> plateau ~14 m with two cliff watchtowers, decks +6.4 m -> pass -> inner basin ~20 m with Hyperia, nine farm fields, a river from a mountain waterfall into a lake, a bridge) closed by 150-300 m mountains and the sea; the diplomatic hall's public gallery (+3 m), banners without society names, trade hall, timber yard and market stalls are our dressing of the hub; the T-head sloops are the physical form of the documented crossing and fire the edge as DANGEROUS+UNKNOWN with a caption that the hull splits in the dead zone (the page gives death in all attempts and only a theoretical landfall); the arcade-machine arrival from Level 25 is placed in the Hyperia plaza because the page does not say where it lands. Dead zone: past z=140 the sea current pulls outward and captions escalate; past z=190 the player dies (not in QA mode). Watching from a tower deck for 6 s shows a dark mass breaking the surface ~1 km offshore (max 3 per visit) and appends an entry to the west tower's watch log. Terrain uses CC0 Poly Haven sparse_grass, coast_sand_01, aerial_rocks_02, dirt_floor, rusty_metal, old_wood_floor textures already in assets/external.
